articles.title: TOISA 2026: Meet the nominees for Cricket Player of the Year (Male)
articles.summary: The Times of India Sports Awards (TOISA) will return for its ninth edition on December 6, 2026, with Dehradun, Uttarakhand, set to host the annual
articles.body: The Times of India Sports Awards (TOISA) will return for its ninth edition on December 6, 2026, with Dehradun, Uttarakhand, set to host the annual celebration of Indian sporting excellence.The awards will recognise outstanding performances across disciplines during a year that featured two major multi-sport events - the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya - alongside world championships and other international competitions.The nominees for Cricket Player of the Year (Male) reflect the breadth of Indian cricket in 2026. Across the season, the shortlisted athletes and teams featured in major events, national and international competitions, and important milestones in their respective disciplines. The shortlist includes Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Jasprit Bumrah, among the contenders whose performances will be recognised at this year's awards.Meet the nominees for the TOISA 2026 Cricket Player of the Year (Male) award.Sanju SamsonAge: 31Key Achievements in 2026:- Named Player of the Tournament at the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026.- Scored 321 runs at an average of 80.25 and strike rate of 199.38 in five innings, as India’s top run-scorer.- Match-defining knockout innings: 97 (50) vs West Indies, 89 (42) vs England in the semi-final, 89 (46) vs New Zealand in the final.- Won the men’s ICC Player of the Month award for March 2026.- Scored an unbeaten 115 off 56 balls against Delhi Capitals, his first century for CSK.- Became the first batter in IPL history to score centuries for three different teams (Delhi Daredevils, Rajasthan Royals, CSK), and the first CSK wicketkeeper to score an IPL century.- Reached 5,000 IPL runs; only AB de Villiers and David Warner got there quicker, making him the fastest Indian.- Member of the India squad that won men’s cricket gold at the 2026 Asian Games.Sanju Samson had a career-defining 2026. He finished as India’s highest run-scorer at the T20 World Cup 2026 and was named Player of the Tournament for his decisive knocks in the knockout stages and the final. He scored 321 runs at an average of 80.25 and a strike rate of 199.38 across five innings. His run began with 97 off 50 balls against West Indies in the Super 8, followed by 89 off 42 against England in the semi-final and 89 off 46 against New Zealand in the final. India became the first team to successfully defend the T20 World Cup title, and Samson was named ICC Player of the Month for March.He then moved to Chennai Super Kings for IPL 2026, hit two centuries and became the fastest Indian to 5,000 IPL runs. In October he was part of India’s Asian Games gold-medal squad.Abhishek SharmaAge: 26Key Achievements in 2026:- Member of the 2026 T20 World Cup-winning India squad.- Scored a 35-ball century in the third T20I during India's tour of New Zealand.- Became the fastest to 5,000 T20 runs.- Unbeaten 135 off 68 balls vs Delhi Capitals in IPL 2026, his second IPL hundred.- Won gold at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.Abhishek Sharma opened 2026 with record-setting hitting against New Zealand. In the first T20I at Nagpur on January 21 he made 84 off 35 balls. He also became the fastest to reach 5,000 runs in T20 cricket during that match. Four days later in Guwahati he hit 68 not out off 20 balls, including a 14-ball fifty, the second-fastest by an Indian in T20Is. He was a member of the India squad that won the 2026 T20 World Cup. In the IPL for Sunrisers Hyderabad, he struck an unbeaten 135 off 68 balls against Delhi Capitals, his first hundred of the season. He top-scored with 61 as India posted 211/6 in the Asian Games final, which India won by 19 runs. He then also scored a 35-ball century in third T20I during India's tour of New Zealand.Jasprit BumrahAge: 32Key Achievements in 2026:- Joint-highest wicket-taker (14) at the 2026 T20 World Cup, alongside Varun Chakravarthy.- Took 4 for 15 in the final, his best T20I figures, to help seal India’s title win.- Won Player of the Match in the final.- Completed 500 international wickets in the semi-final, becoming the eighth Indian to do so.- Took his 150th ODI wicket in the first ODI against England at Edgbaston.- Joined Shakib Al Hasan and Tim Southee as the only players with 200 Test, 150 ODI and 100 T20I wickets.- Became India’s highest ODI wicket-taker in England, with 31.- Took 2 for 7 in two overs in the Asian Games semi-final against Sri Lanka, who were bowled out for 45.- Won gold at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.Jasprit Bumrah was India’s leading bowler as they retained the T20 World Cup. He finished as joint-highest wicket-taker with 14 wickets in eight innings, at an average of 12.42 and an economy rate of 6.21. In the final against New Zealand at his home ground in Ahmedabad, he took career-best T20I figures of 4 for 15. In the semi-final against England he took his 500th international wicket, dismissing captain Harry Brook. In July he returned to ODIs after 968 days and took his 150th ODI wicket. That also made him India’s highest ODI wicket-taker on English soil. He later returned to T20 action at the Asian Games and helped India win gold.Shubman GillAge: 27Key Achievements in 2026:- Led India to an innings-and-300-run win, their biggest-ever Test victory.- Fastest Indian captain to 1,000 Test runs by time taken, in 351 days, breaking Sachin Tendulkar’s mark of 405 days.- That innings was his sixth hundred as India’s Test captain.- Led India to a 1-0 Test series win in Sri Lanka- Scored consecutive centuries in the first two ODIs of the home series against West Indies, 110 and then 223 not out.- The 223* came off 133 balls, with the double century reached in 117 balls.- Led Gujarat Titans to the IPL 2026 final.- Scored 732 runs in IPL 2026 (average 45.75, strike rate 196.22), the second-highest aggregate of the tournament.Shubman Gill captained India in both Tests and ODIs in 2026 and led Gujarat Titans in the IPL. In the one-off Test against Afghanistan he scored 126 off 177 balls and completed 1,000 Test runs as captain. India won by an innings and 300 runs, their biggest-ever Test victory. He then led India to a 1-0 series win in Sri Lanka. In September he hit the fastest double century in ODI history, an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, as India chased down 406 against West Indies; that record was later bettered by Harry Brook. Earlier, he led Gujarat Titans to the IPL 2026 final, where they lost to Royal Challengers Bengaluru. He scored 732 runs in 16 matches in that campaignIshan KishanAge: 28Key Achievements in 2026:- Scored his maiden T20I century, 103 off 43 balls against New Zealand in the fifth T20I on 31 January.- Scored 317 runs in nine innings at a strike rate of 193.29 at the T20 World Cup, with three fifties including a 25-ball 54 in the final against New Zealand.- Scored 61 off 24 balls against Namibia, the first fifty by an Indian wicketkeeper in T20 World Cup history, and 77 off 40 against Pakistan.- Part of India’s title-winning side, which beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the Ahmedabad final on 8 March.- Scored 602 runs at a strike rate of 182.42 in IPL 2026, the most productive season of his IPL career.- Scored 270 off 334 balls (30 fours, 7 sixes) for East Zone in the Duleep Trophy final against South Zone.- East Zone won the title on first-innings lead, ending a 13-year wait.Ishan Kishan had a standout 2026 across formats after returning to India’s T20I side. At the T20 World Cup, which India won, he scored 317 runs at a strike rate of 193.29 and became the first Indian wicketkeeper to score a fifty in the tournament’s history. In the IPL, he scored 602 runs for Sunrisers Hyderabad and captained the side early in the season. articles.title: 'We should be so angry': Ashwin's fiery reaction to India's Wellington Test draw
articles.summary: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin was disappointed with India's decision to settle for a draw against New Zealand in the opening Test in
articles.body: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin was disappointed with India's decision to settle for a draw against New Zealand in the opening Test in Wellington, questioning the lack of urgency shown by Shubman Gill's side during the final stages of the match.With New Zealand still trailing by 113 runs and having lost five wickets, India had around 15 overs left on the final day to push for a victory. However, the visitors decided to shake hands, allowing the hosts to escape with a draw despite being in a difficult position for much of the contest.Ashwin felt India missed the aggressive approach that characterised the Virat Kohli era, arguing that the team should have continued attacking rather than allowing the New Zealand batters to settle into a comfortable rhythm.Speaking on his podcast Ash Ki Baat, Ashwin pointed to the contrast in the way India approached the closing stages of a match under Kohli's leadership.“I think one thing we can learn from Virat Kohli’s captaincy — a draw was also possible, you can never say another bowler or another captain would have won the match — but I’ll only say this: urgency helps," Ashwin said.He also referred to Daryl Mitchell's relaxed demeanour at the crease, highlighting how the New Zealand batter was comfortable interacting with teammates and opposition players despite his side being under pressure.“See, Daryl Mitchell was batting, he was doing that sight-screen drama, going to the captain, talking to our players, laughing and smiling. That was never the case. Smiling and laughing doesn’t happen in our team. When we’re on top it happens, but when we’re chasing a result we’re ready to fight, because otherwise the batsmen go into a comfort zone," he added.Ashwin believed India should have used the remaining 15 overs to continue hunting for wickets, even if that meant turning to the spinners and placing attacking fielders around the bat.When asked whether extending the bowlers' workload by another hour, particularly with the second Test still to come, was justified, Ashwin insisted that such demands were an integral part of playing Test cricket.“Test players must be ready for this demand. In this Test match Bumrah bowled long spells," Ashwin said.He suggested that India could have brought the spinners into the attack, lifted the atmosphere at the ground and maintained pressure on the opposition rather than calling off the contest.“If you feel Bumrah shouldn’t do extra, bowl spinners, raise the crowd… We dominated this Test match, but you’ve not nailed them, right? Nobody will give us points for dominating the Test match. Points come for winning. People will say you played a very good Test match, but didn’t take 20 wickets — we won’t get points for good cricket… Especially with New Zealand sitting on top of the WTC table — after putting them in such trouble, we should be so angry for pulling ourselves back. And that is my point," he said.Ashwin compared India's inability to finish the job to a runner failing to complete the final stretch of a marathon after having controlled most of the race. However, he was careful not to single out the bowlers for the missed opportunity.Instead, he felt the team needed to display greater intent through aggressive field placements and sustained pressure. Considering the flat nature of the surface, Ashwin believed the bowlers had done their job and that the urgency needed to come from the team's overall approach.How the Wellington Test unfoldedIndia had put themselves in a commanding position after declaring their first innings at 702/9, having bowled New Zealand out for 368.The hosts began the final day at 119/2, still 233 runs behind, but India managed only three wickets during the day's play. Devon Conway (65) and Rachin Ravindra (37) were dismissed in the first session, with Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna providing the breakthroughs.Anshul Kamboj then removed Tom Blundell for 15 off 54 deliveries, but India could not make further inroads for a prolonged period.A missed run-out opportunity involving Mitchell, after Akash Deep failed to collect the ball cleanly, proved costly for the visitors. Mitchell remained unbeaten on 49 off 186 balls, while Glenn Phillips, who had scored a century in the first innings, finished unbeaten on 26 off 126 deliveries.The pair faced 259 balls together to ensure New Zealand survived the remaining overs, finishing at 239/5 in 120 overs.The result left India with a draw despite their dominance for large parts of the match, while New Zealand managed to salvage valuable World Test Championship points.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. They eventually finished at 239/5, with Daryl Mitchell (49 not out off 187 balls) and Glenn Phillips (26 not out off 126 balls) frustrating the Indian attack with a determined defensive display.The draw further dented India's WTC final qualification hopes, with their points percentage dropping from 51.52 to 50. articles.title: ILT20: Babar Azam shines on debut with match-winning 86 as Desert Vipers beat Warriorz
articles.summary: Babar Azam made an impressive start to his ILT20 career, scoring a match-winning 86 to help defending champions Desert Vipers beat Sharjah Warriorz by six
articles.body: Babar Azam made an impressive start to his ILT20 career, scoring a match-winning 86 to help defending champions Desert Vipers beat Sharjah Warriorz by six wickets in Season 5 at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Monday.Chasing 167, Babar anchored the innings with 86 off just 51 balls, hitting 13 fours. His knock, which included a record number of fours in the league, helped the Vipers reach 167/4 in 17.3 overs and register their first win of the season.The Vipers' bowlers had earlier restricted the Warriorz to 166 in 20 overs. Shadab Khan led the attack with 3/18, while Khuzaima Tanveer picked up three wickets for 31 runs.This was also the Vipers' seventh consecutive victory over the Warriorz.Babar, Clarke put Vipers in controlThe Vipers started their chase positively, but Junaid Siddique removed Fakhar Zaman (15 off 10) in the fourth over. Waqar Salamkheil then struck with his first ball of the match, bowling Andries Gous (13 off 5) in the seventh over.The Vipers were 70/2 at that stage, but Babar took charge and completed his half-century in just 31 balls in the 10th over.He then joined hands with Joe Clarke to build an important partnership. The pair added 82 runs for the third wicket, bringing the Vipers close to the target.Clarke scored 35 off 27 balls before Adam Milne dismissed him in the 16th over. Milne also removed Babar in the same over, but the damage had already been done.Shimron Hetmyer (4 not out) and captain Shadab Khan (8 not out off 5) completed the chase as the Vipers reached their target with 15 balls to spare.Walter's half-century goes in vainEarlier, Paul Walter played a fighting knock of 75 off 43 balls to give the Warriorz a strong start. However, the Vipers' bowlers pulled things back with regular wickets.Tom Curran provided the first breakthrough in the third over, dismissing Tim Seifert (17 off 9) to leave the Warriorz at 34/1.Walter continued to attack and reached his half-century in 30 balls with a six off Mujeeb Ur Rahman in the 10th over. He added 68 runs off 48 balls with James Vince before Shadab broke the partnership in the 11th over. Vince was dismissed for 23 off 22 balls, caught by Hetmyer.Shadab struck twice again in the 13th over. He bowled Brandon McMullen (2 off 6) before dismissing Warriorz captain Sikandar Raza (0 off 2) two balls later.Naseem Shah then removed Walter in the 14th over, leaving the Warriorz at 128/5.Tanveer joined the wicket-taking effort in the 16th over by dismissing Mohammad Nabi (3 off 8). He picked up two more wickets, one in the 18th over and another in the final over, as the Warriorz were bowled out for 166.Babar, Raza reflect on the resultBabar was named Player of the Match for his match-winning innings. The Pakistan batter was pleased to contribute to the team's first victory of the season on his ILT20 debut."It's my first match and the team's first win. We planned the first six overs, played cricketing shots and stayed positive, and then we built partnerships and the innings. The way our fast bowlers pulled things back was fantastic," Babar said.Warriorz captain Sikandar Raza felt his team lost control of the match because of Shadab's bowling spell and the failure of the middle order to score enough runs."We lost momentum in the first half and couldn't get it back. Our top three were nice to watch, but one spell from Shadab changed the game. The middle order hasn't fired in this game or the last, so we're missing runs from the middle and lower order. We thought we'd get the momentum back with the ball, but they had such a brilliant start that by the time we did, it was too late," Raza said.Brief scoresSharjah Warriorz: 166 all out in 20 overs (Paul Walter 75, James Vince 23, George Linde 14; Shadab Khan 3/18, Khuzaima Tanveer 3/31)Desert Vipers: 167/4 in 17.3 overs (Babar Azam 86, Joe Clarke 35, Fakhar Zaman 15; Adam Milne 2/42, Waqar Salamkheil 1/26)Player of the Match: Babar Azam (Desert Vipers)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A Long Walk Back! Another draw dents WTC Final hopes as Mitchell, Phillips stonewall India on lifeless Basin pitch
articles.summary: \"Catch it!
articles.body: "Catch it! Boom bhai,” yelled India skipper Shubman Gill from cover as New Zealand’s Daryl Mitchell jammed the bat down on a cleverly bowled slower one from Jasprit Bumrah half an hour before lunch on Day 5 of the first Test at the Basin Reserve on Monday.The excitement levels among Indian players were high at that stage as New Zealand had been reduced to 139/4 and the visitors had picked up both the overnight not-out batters, Devon Convoy and Rachin Ravindra and both Mitchell and keeper-batter Tom Blundell were new to the wicket.Bumrah, who was in his second spell (strangely, he bowled only 11 overs on the final day, spread across four spells of three, three, three and two), replied with a mix of exasperation and irritation, “Kaise pakdu? Hain? (How?)”. Someone else then chimed in, “Udd ke (By flying)”.It reflected the team’s expectations from the pacer. They wanted him to be Superman. He was anything but that on Monday.A lifeless Basin Reserve pitch and the resolve of two natural attacking batters, Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips, who turned into strokeless wonders, helped the hosts bat for 120 overs in their second innings to salvage a draw. The Kiwis finished on 239/5 before both teams agreed for a stalemate.Mitchell remained unbeaten on 49 off 187 balls and Phillips 26 off 126, their unbroken sixthwicket partnership consuming 258 deliveries. New Zealand scored only 120 runs in 75 overs on the final day. Runs, though, were irrelevant. Batting time, a rapidly diminishing skill, was everything.This draw though, has made India’s difficult path to the World Test Championship final rockier.Their points percentage slipped from 51.52 to 50, leaving them fourth. New Zealand dropped to third at 66.67, behind Australia (69.23), with South Africa leading at 75.India began the final day needing eight wickets, with New Zealand 119 for two and still 233 runs adrift. Considering the pitch had barely deteriorated, India needed inspiration from Bumrah and ingenuity from Gill.They got neither.Conway and Ravindra gave away team plans early in the piece as they scored 13 runs in more than 10 overs as they defied Bumrah, Akash and Anshul Kamboj in their first spell.Washington Sundar finally provided the breakthrough. Bowling into the wind, the offspinner found 63 cms of drift in to draw Conway forward as the inside edge deflected off his pad for Rishabh Pant to complete an acrobatic catch. Pant had been asking Sundar to aim at the rough on the off-stump.However, Conway’s 65 (165) had already eaten into the bowlers’ energy levels.Prasidh Krishna was not one of those as he produced a much better spell prior to lunch. A slightly short-of-length delivery cramped Ravindra 37(129 balls), whose half-push, half-drive flew to KL Rahul at gully.After lunch, Kamboj found a faint edge from Tom Blundell that Pant pouched standing up to the stumps. India needed DRS to confirm the dismissal. At 176 for five, dreams of a win were still on.However, Mitchell and Phillips simply refused to budge. India took the second new ball after 82 overs, but even that offered no help. Prasidh induced a bat-pad opportunity from Mitchell, but India, curiously, had no short-leg in position.The missed chance that will hurt more, though, is the run-out opportunity that came off the first ball of the third over after lunch as Akash Deep fluffed a straightforward collection with Mitchell stranded more than halfway down the pitch. “Mark that down,” Ian Smith said on air as a furious Gill yelled out a Punjabi expletive.Mitchell and Phillips were happy defending. As a result, India bowled eight successive maidens from over No. 88 to 95. India should ask themselves though how badly did they want to win. Could they have been more adventurous with their fields and tactics?This was the second successive Test they had failed to close out from a winning position. They needed four wickets on the final day against Sri Lanka at SSC and ran into Sonal Dinusha.Read that as 16 WTC points gone in what has been a disappointing cycle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Who's got the mints?': Fresh allegations of ball-tampering during 2018 Pakistan Test put Justin Langer, Tim Paine in spotlight
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A new allegation has surfaced in the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A new allegation has surfaced in the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. Australian players reportedly discussed using mints to tamper with the ball during a Test against Pakistan, just six months after the infamous incident in Cape Town.An investigation by sports broadcaster Gerard Whateley claims that former coach Justin Langer and then-captain Tim Paine stepped in to stop the players during the first Test against Pakistan in Dubai in October 2018.Players allegedly discussed using mintsAccording to Whateley's report, one player asked: “Who’s got the mints? Who’s doing the ball today?”.A new member of the team reportedly reacted by saying: “You’re f*ing kidding me. We’re not doing that sh** again.”Despite the objection, a substitute fielder was allegedly asked to go to the dressing room and get mints. Paine then intervened and gestured to the player to return to his seat.Langer also reportedly confronted the players after the day's play. The former coach used a baggy green cap to express his anger.Paine and Langer take a standAfter the Cape Town scandal, Australia had reportedly decided that players would not be allowed to take lollies onto the field. Paine had also assured the support staff that he would not allow players to use them on the ball while he was captain.Whateley's report claims that the incident in Dubai was the last time Australian players tried to manipulate the ball during a match.Fresh claims bring Sandpapergate back into focusThe latest allegations have once again raised questions about how much senior players knew about the original ball-tampering scandal in 2018.Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were suspended after Bancroft was caught using sandpaper on the ball during the Test against South Africa in Cape Town.Whateley's investigation also reveals an alleged confrontation between Mitchell Marsh and Warner at the team hotel. Marsh reportedly asked Warner to take responsibility for his role in the plan instead of letting Bancroft carry the blame.Sources quoted in the report said the incident exposed differences within the Australian team. Some players did not agree with the idea of the entire squad taking collective responsibility.The latest allegations have added another chapter to the dispute, which was brought back into focus by Bancroft's recent statement and Usman Khawaja's claim that the entire team knew about the plan.Pat Cummins has repeatedly denied knowing about the sandpaper plot. Josh Hazlewood has also defended the current Australia Test captain amid the renewed controversy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Shubman Gill reveals why Team India cancelled planned activity after drawn Wellington Test
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's bowlers had to put in a long shift during the drawn first Test against New Zealand in Wellington.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's bowlers had to put in a long shift during the drawn first Test against New Zealand in Wellington. With the attack delivering close to 250 overs across the two innings, the team management decided to cancel a planned team activity in Christchurch.India captain Shubman Gill said the players deserved a break after such a demanding effort. He also promised that the bowlers would be taken out for dinner."Our bowlers have put in so many overs, we will definitely take them (out for a dinner). We had a team activity but after bowling so many overs it stands cancelled," Gill said.Bowlers deliver close to 250 oversThe Indian bowling attack had a busy Test match, with the bowlers delivering 121 overs in New Zealand's first innings and another 120 in the second.Jasprit Bumrah bowled 49 overs across the two innings and picked up five wickets. Akash Deep bowled 43 overs and took three wickets, while Anshul Kamboj delivered 45 overs and claimed three wickets.Prasidh Krishna bowled 45 overs and took three wickets. Washington Sundar also put in a long shift, bowling 55 overs and picking up one wicket.Gill said India had started the final day well but could not make the most of their opportunities."We were very good in first session, were looking to get into the tail. Got two half chances and maybe could have been different. Energy was good and everyone was enjoying," he said.Gill wants ICC to review saliva banGill also urged the ICC to reconsider its ban on using saliva to shine the ball. He said the Kookaburra ball was becoming soft too quickly, making it difficult for bowlers to take wickets on pitches offering little help.New Zealand batted for 75 overs on the final day, scoring 120 runs for the loss of three wickets. They finished their second innings at 239 for five, and neither team could force a result."We are way past Covid times. There was a rule that you can't apply saliva to shine the ball. It's been 7-8 years now, I still don't understand why they are not allowing it," Gill said.The India captain said the ball had lost its hardness early in the match."Our first ball, I think after 25-30 overs, the ball became very soft. I think they also complained," he said."We saw this in England as well. In the first 3-4 matches, we gave a slightly different ball in the Oval,"Soft ball makes life difficult for bowlersGill also raised concerns about the quality of the Kookaburra ball. He said a softer ball makes it harder for fielders to take catches behind the wicket, especially when the pitch does not offer much movement."I don't know if the quality of the balls has come down or what happened. But in such conditions, if there is no help from the wicket, and the ball also becomes soft, then it becomes very difficult for the bowlers to take wickets," he said."They don't carry the edges. So, the caught-behind dismissal becomes harder. If there is not so much movement in the pitch, then the LBW remains on hold."Gill felt allowing saliva would help teams maintain the ball's condition for a longer period, particularly on flat pitches."And on the saliva, yes, I do believe that teams should be allowed to use saliva. It was a rule that was made effective during COVID. I think we are long past that," he said."The condition of the ball, if you're not shining the ball or if you're not able to maintain the ball well, especially on wickets like these, it makes the job of the bowlers very difficult."He said India had faced a similar problem during their 2025 tour of England, where the ball became soft early in the innings."Ideally, we understand after 50 overs, the ball obviously will go soft. But if the ball is going soft after 25-30 overs or it's going out of shape and you're also not able to maintain the ball and use saliva, then it's a very difficult job for the bowlers," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I'm really disappointed': Matthew Hayden takes aim at 2018 Australian side over Sandpapergate
articles.summary: Former Australia opener Matthew Hayden has expressed his disappointment with the 2018 Australian side over the infamous Sandpapergate controversy, saying
articles.body: Former Australia opener Matthew Hayden has expressed his disappointment with the 2018 Australian side over the infamous Sandpapergate controversy, saying the team failed to uphold one of the defining characteristics of its cricketing culture – confronting problems collectively inside the dressing room.With the ball-tampering scandal back in the spotlight following fresh revelations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft, Hayden believes the focus will eventually shift back to cricket, with Australia having several important assignments ahead, including the Border-Gavaskar Trophy (BGT) in India from January 21, 2027.However, while backing Australia's competitive spirit and its traditional winning culture, Hayden was particularly critical of the players involved in the 2018 episode for not resolving the matter internally."Will Australia want to win? That's my first question. I can, hand on heart, tell you that Australia will not only be competitive, but will also want to win. In the context of cricket, Australia has largely been very fair in the way it has gone about its cricketing culture. Very little has disrupted the nature of the Australian winning culture. It's a very in-your-face culture. It will confront issues inside the change room collectively. That's why I'm really disappointed in this 2018 mob that couldn't do it," Hayden said on JioStar.Hayden backs Cummins' handling of controversyHayden also praised current Australia captain Pat Cummins for addressing the renewed questions surrounding the scandal head-on, describing his willingness to face scrutiny and present his version of events as a position of strength.Cummins had dismissed Khawaja's allegations as "utter nonsense" during a press conference, insisting that the bowling group was unaware of the ball-tampering plan. His comments subsequently triggered another round of debate, with Bancroft publishing a lengthy column in The West Australian.Hayden, however, feels the game has largely moved on from the controversy and that the focus will soon return to performances on the field."Largely, the game has already moved on. Pat Cummins, as you can see, is very keen to embrace his leadership style. He came out with an hour-and-a-bit press conference and said, 'Guys, this is what I've got to say. Ask me any question you want. Challenge me? Sure. Then I'm telling you this is my account of it.' That position is one of strength, and the game has moved on and will move on very quickly. The cricket will speak for itself, and it will speak volumes," he added.Sandpapergate resurfaces ahead of busy Australia scheduleThe controversy has returned to the headlines after Khawaja, in his autobiography Sabr, claimed that every member of the Australian squad knew about the use of sandpaper during the infamous 2018 South Africa tour.Cummins rejected the allegation, prompting Bancroft, who was caught on television cameras using sandpaper during the Cape Town Test, to revisit the episode in a 4,000-word column published in The West Australian on Wednesday.Bancroft questioned the bowling group's claims that they had no knowledge of the plan. He also recalled a discussion during the tea break on the second day of the Port Elizabeth Test, alleging that bowling coach David Saker and head coach Darren Lehmann were present when David Warner suggested using sandpaper to roughen one side of the ball.Hayden, meanwhile, believes Australia's packed international calendar will leave little room for the controversy to dominate the conversation for long. The team is scheduled to face England and New Zealand before travelling to India for the next BGT."We have the series against England, followed by four Test matches against New Zealand, which will famously be played during the Christmas and New Year window, before the BGT. January 21 is the commencement of the BGT; I think, so things will move very quickly after that. There is plenty of cricket to focus on," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 19 sixes, 181 runs! Priyansh Arya rewrites T20 history, breaks KL Rahul's record with stunning knock
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi captain Priyansh Arya produced a breathtaking batting display on Tuesday, smashing a sensational 181 off just 68 balls against Tamil Nadu
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi captain Priyansh Arya produced a breathtaking batting display on Tuesday, smashing a sensational 181 off just 68 balls against Tamil Nadu in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy to rewrite the T20 record books. He became the highest-scoring Indian batter in T20 cricket history, surpassing KL Rahul's previous record, while also equalling the world record for the most sixes in a single T20 innings.The left-handed opener smashed an astonishing 19 sixes and 7 fours to power Delhi to a mammoth 275/5 in their 20 overs at the Daly College Ground in Indore. His 181 is now the second-highest individual score in men's T20 cricket, behind South African Lhuan-dre Pretorius, who scored an unbeaten 188 off 79 balls for Titans against Knights in the CSA Pro20 Cup in October 2026.Arya's innings eclipsed Rahul's 152 not out, scored earlier this year for Delhi Capitals against Punjab Kings in IPL 2026, to become the highest individual T20 score by an Indian.36-ball hundred, 19 sixes: Arya goes on record-breaking rampageSent in to bat by Tamil Nadu, Delhi suffered an early setback when Yash Dhull departed for eight in the third over. However, Arya ensured that the early wicket did little to derail Delhi's innings as he took the attack to the opposition bowlers.He found some support from Nitish Rana, with the duo adding 118 runs for the second wicket. Rana contributed 18 off 17 deliveries, but Arya did most of the damage at the other end.The Delhi captain raced to his hundred in just 36 deliveries, hammering 12 sixes and four boundaries in the process. He continued his assault after reaching the milestone, going past Rahul's Indian record of 152 not out before eventually falling for a remarkable 181 off 68 balls.His 19 sixes took him level with Finn Allen's record, set in June 2025, while putting him past Chris Gayle and Estonia's Sahil Chauhan, who had smashed 18 sixes each. Arya now shares the record for the most sixes hit by a batter in a single T20 innings.Arya's 181 takes Delhi to 275/5Arya's extraordinary knock provided the foundation for Delhi's imposing total of 275/5 in 20 overs. The next-best contribution came from Anuj Rawat, who remained unbeaten on 29, underlining just how much of Delhi's scoring was driven by their captain.Highest individual scores in T20 cricketLhuan-dre Pretorius - 188* (79)Priyansh Arya - 181 (68)Chris Gayle - 175* (66)Aaron Finch - 172 (76)Hamza Khan - 164* (65)Rahul's previous Indian record had come in spectacular circumstances as well. His unbeaten 152 for Delhi Capitals against Punjab Kings in Delhi earlier in IPL 2026 featured 16 fours and nine sixes, helping DC post 264/2. However, the mammoth total was not enough to secure victory, with Punjab Kings chasing it down with seven balls to spare.Interestingly, Arya was on the opposite side of that contest and played a significant role in the successful chase, smashing 43 off just 17 balls. He added 126 for the opening wicket with Prabhsimran Singh, who top-scored with 76 off 26 deliveries, as Punjab completed a remarkable chase.On Tuesday, however, Arya ensured that his name would stand above Rahul's in the Indian T20 record books, producing an innings that also rewrote the global six-hitting record.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A captain Tilak Varma made three changes to the playing XI for their crucial Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 Group B match against the United Arab Emirates in Doha on Tuesday.UAE captain Basil Hameed won the toss and elected to bat at the University of Doha for Science and Technology.India brought in Prabhsimran Singh, Harsh Dubey and Arshad Khan in place of Ayush Badoni, Vipraj Nigam and Prince Yadav.Asia Cup Rising Stars: Badoni, Nigam, Prince dropped after Pakistan defeatThe changes came after India A suffered a 48-run defeat against Pakistan A in their previous match on Sunday.India had bowled Pakistan out for 313 in 49.2 overs but failed to chase down the target. Badoni and Vipraj both had disappointing outings with the bat, getting out for ducks.However, Vipraj did contribute with the ball, taking two wickets for 46 runs in his eight overs. Prince Yadav also picked up two wickets but conceded 60 runs in 9.2 overs.India will now look for a stronger all-round performance against the UAE.Asia Cup Rising Stars: India A's semifinal hopes at stakeThe defeat against Pakistan has put pressure on India's semifinal hopes, but they remain in contention for a place in the last four.India A have two points from two matches and need a win against the UAE to reach four points and secure qualification.Pakistan A have already booked their semifinal spot after winning both their group matches. The top two teams from Group B will advance to the semifinals, scheduled for November 26 and 27.Asia Cup Rising Stars: Where do India A stand in the points table?Pakistan A are at the top of Group B with four points from two matches. India A and Nepal have two points each, while the UAE are yet to open their account.Nepal kept their qualification hopes alive with a six-wicket win over the UAE on Sunday. Pakistan A then defeated India A to seal their place in the semifinals.India's positive net run rate of +2.580 gives them an advantage over Nepal and could prove important if the teams finish level on points.How can India A qualify for the semifinals?India A have several possible routes to the last four, with their match against the UAE playing a key role.1. India A beat UAE and Pakistan A beat NepalThis is the simplest route. A win will take India A to four points and guarantee them a semifinal spot, regardless of the result of the other match.2. India A beat UAE and Nepal beat Pakistan AIn this situation, India A, Pakistan A and Nepal will all finish with four points. Net run rate will decide the final standings.India A will have an advantage because of their 306-run win over Nepal earlier in the tournament. Their current net run rate of +2.580 is much better than Nepal's -2.461.3. They will still qualify if Pakistan A beat Nepal, as Nepal will remain on two points.4. UAE beat India A and Pakistan A beat NepalA defeat will make India's task difficult but will not end their campaign immediately.Pakistan A will finish with six points, while India A, Nepal and the UAE will all have two points. Net run rate will then decide the second semifinal spot. India's current advantage over Nepal could prove crucial, but the margin of defeat against the UAE will matter.5. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: After a frustrating stalemate at the Basin Reserve, where only 24 wickets fell across five days and the pitch gradually became slower and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: After a frustrating stalemate at the Basin Reserve, where only 24 wickets fell across five days and the pitch gradually became slower and lower, New Zealand all-rounder Daryl Mitchell is expecting a more competitive contest between bat and ball at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. Mitchell believes the surface for the second Test against India, starting Friday, could offer more bounce and give the bowlers a better chance of making an impact.The first Test ended in a draw after New Zealand fought hard to deny India a victory on the final day. Mitchell, who remained unbeaten on 49, acknowledged that the Basin Reserve surface had not behaved as expected despite its generous covering of grass at the start."I think the nature of the base and surface at Basin Reserve is such that it usually looks pretty green at the start. We probably didn't expect it to get that slow and low over the course of five days, but now we're here at Hagley and I'm sure there might be a bit of bounce in this one," Mitchell said.'We were both pretty happy to do so': Mitchell on final-day drawIndia threw everything at New Zealand on the final day, pushing for a victory before the two sides eventually agreed to shake hands with around an hour of play remaining. Mitchell admitted that the Black Caps were equally relieved to settle for a draw after a demanding five days, particularly given the workload on the bowlers."Look, you could see the amount of effort they were putting in throughout the day. It takes a toll on the bowlers' bodies, and it's a big series as well. When they wanted to shake hands, we were both pretty happy to do so," Mitchell said.The 35-year-old also credited New Zealand's collective character for standing firm and batting out the final day to frustrate India."I think it's just the character of the group to keep fighting as much as we can and keep giving to that Black Cap. That's sort of what we pride ourselves on, and it's nice to show it again," he said.Familiar Hagley Oval offers New Zealand confidenceMitchell will be particularly pleased to return to Christchurch, where he has played extensively over the years. The all-rounder believes familiarity with the venue and its conditions will help New Zealand prepare for the second Test."Yeah, it's cool to be home and to wake up in your own bed. The morning of Test matches is always nice, looking forward to it.""A number of us have played a lot of cricket at Hagley Oval over the last decade or so, so we know what conditions to expect. It's a beautiful ground to play Test cricket at, and we're all looking forward to it," Mitchell said.While the drawn opener provided positives for both sides, Mitchell acknowledged that New Zealand's bowlers needed time to recover before the next challenge."Both teams will take a lot of positives out of that Test match. For us, it's our first hit-out in Test cricket for a while. I know the bowlers were probably a bit sore a few days ago, but they've got a few days' rest now to get ready to go again. So, yeah, look, it's only going to help us going forward," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Not everyone did it': Merv Hughes hits back at Lehmann's 150-year ball-tampering claim amid Sandpapergate row
articles.summary: Former Australia fast bowler Merv Hughes has strongly disputed Darren Lehmann's claim that ball-tampering has been part of cricket for 150 years,
articles.body: Former Australia fast bowler Merv Hughes has strongly disputed Darren Lehmann's claim that ball-tampering has been part of cricket for 150 years, insisting that the practice was not widespread and accusing some former players of trying to justify their actions.The Sandpapergate controversy has resurfaced following fresh revelations by Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft about the 2018 South Africa tour. Lehmann, Australia's head coach during the scandal, recently claimed that ball-tampering had been happening for generations, while maintaining that he was unaware of plans to use sandpaper during the Cape Town Test."I probably take offence to a lot of the podcasts going around and a lot of the past players (saying) ‘Oh, everyone did it’. Well, mate, not everyone did it," Hughes told CODE Sports."... I didn’t see it as a selector, and I didn’t see it as a player," he added.Lehmann had made his comments during an interview with ABC radio ahead of Australia's recent first T20I against England."I can’t remember David Warner raising the possibility of using sandpaper," Lehmann had said."You do know ball tampering is going on because it’s been happening for 150 years," the 56-year-old added."It’s just how it’s being done ... I can only speak to what I know, and I know ball tampering was a big part of the game of cricket. That doesn’t make it right either, but that’s the case," he said.'The guys who did it are trying to justify themselves'Hughes, who played 53 Tests for Australia, all under former captain Allan Border, said he never witnessed ball-tampering during his playing career. He also suggested that Border would not have tolerated any attempt to cross the line."It wasn’t ICC or Cricket Australia that got worried about it as players; it would have been Allan Border. If we did something untoward or outside the rules with AB, it turned around pretty quickly. So it never happened," Hughes said.He also recalled checking with former Victoria teammate Ian Wrigglesworth about whether such practices had taken place at the state level."I just had to talk to (former Victorian Sheffield Shield all-rounder) Ian Wrigglesworth over the last couple of days ... I said, ‘mate, can you ever remember it happening at Victoria when we played?’ He said, ‘No, that didn’t happen'," he added.The former Australia selector, who served from 2005 to 2010, was particularly critical of attempts to portray ball-tampering as an accepted part of the game."It almost sounds to me like the guys who did it are trying to justify themselves for doing it," he said.Hughes backs bans handed to Smith, Warner and BancroftHughes also defended the sanctions imposed on Steve Smith, David Warner and Bancroft following the 2018 scandal. Smith and Warner received 12-month bans, while Bancroft was suspended for nine months."While the punishments were harsh, what they had to do was set down a punishment that would stop future Australian players from ever thinking about doing it again. I think they’ve definitely done that, but it sort of raised its ugly head, and it’s just a big one on who do you believe," he added.The latest exchange comes amid renewed scrutiny of the episode. Khawaja, in his autobiography Sabr, claimed that every member of the Australian squad knew about the use of sandpaper. Captain Pat Cummins rejected the allegation, while Bancroft subsequently questioned the bowling group's claims that they had no knowledge of the plan in a lengthy column published in The West Australian.Bancroft also recalled a discussion during the tea break of the Port Elizabeth Test, alleging that Lehmann and bowling coach David Saker were present when Warner suggested using sandpaper to roughen one side of the ball.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Teams were playing out Bumrah': Irfan Pathan explains how Arshdeep's MI arrival changes  things
articles.summary: Mumbai Indians have made a significant statement ahead of the IPL 2027 auction by bringing in India's left-arm pace spearhead Arshdeep Singh in a
articles.body: Mumbai Indians have made a significant statement ahead of the IPL 2027 auction by bringing in India's left-arm pace spearhead Arshdeep Singh in a blockbuster trade with Punjab Kings. The five-time champions have also parted ways with New Zealand veteran Trent Boult, a move that former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan believes makes complete sense given Arshdeep's arrival.Arshdeep joined MI at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore, while Mumbai Indians traded their captain Hardik Pandya to PBKS for the same amount ahead of the retention deadline.Irfan Pathan explains why MI let Trent Boult goSpeaking on JioStar's 'IPL 2027 Retentions', Pathan said, "With Arshdeep Singh coming into Mumbai Indians’ bowling line-up, it makes complete sense to let Trent Boult go. Boult is an overseas left-armer, and MI now have an Indian left-armer in place. Deepak Chahar not being here is understandable because over the last five or six years, he has rarely played a full season, and MI have already secured their new-ball bowler."While ex-batter Abhinav Mukund also highlighted how a strong bowling combination has traditionally played a pivotal role in Mumbai Indians' successful IPL campaigns. He cited the partnerships involving Lasith Malinga, Jasprit Bumrah and Mitchell McClenaghan as examples of the team's successful bowling formula."A strong bowling combination has almost been a feature of their title-winning runs. When they won, it was Malinga, then Malinga and Bumrah together, then Bumrah and Mitch McClenaghan for a while. You always had that support bowler to the primary bowler."Pathan further pointed out that opposition teams had increasingly adopted a cautious approach against Bumrah in recent seasons, choosing to target the other bowlers instead of taking risks against India's premier fast bowler."Over the last couple of years, teams were playing out Bumrah. They were not giving him wickets, and they said, ‘we are happy to take you for 30, but we will go after the other bowlers’. Now it will not happen with Arshdeep in the mix. They need to figure out who bowls in the middle now, but it is a better problem to have than what they did last season," he added.Mumbai Indians' Retention List Ahead Of IPL 2027 AuctionMI retained players: Arshdeep Singh, Ashwani Kumar, Corbin Bosch, Jasprit Bumrah, Mitchell Santner, Naman Dhir, Quinton de Kock, Raghu Sharma, Raj Angad Bawa, Rohit Sharma, Ryan Rickelton, Shardul Thakur, Sherfane Rutherford, Suryakumar Yadav, Tilak Varma and Will Jacks.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Will be the greatest Test player India has seen': R Ashwin's massive praise for Rishabh Pant
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin believes Rishabh Pant has the potential to become \"the greatest Test player that India has seen\", provided the wicketkeeper-batter
articles.body: Ravichandran Ashwin believes Rishabh Pant has the potential to become "the greatest Test player that India has seen", provided the wicketkeeper-batter applies himself consistently. Ashwin lavished praise on Pant after India drew the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington, with the left-hander producing a sensational 128 off 153 balls in the first innings.Pant's knock also saw him break Adam Gilchrist's world record for the most runs by a designated wicketkeeper-batter in away Tests.However, it was not just Pant's batting that impressed Ashwin. The former India off-spinner was particularly taken by his chatter from behind the stumps, which added life to a Test played on a flat pitch and helped make an otherwise dull contest a better spectacle."In this game, I became a bigger fan of Rishabh Pant's keeping than his batting," Ashwin said. "There was no atmosphere in the game — he created atmosphere in the game. The chirping from behind, all of that he did. If Rishabh applies himself, he will be the greatest Test player that India has seen," he added.Application has been a longstanding talking point when it comes to Pant's batting. An aggressive approach has made him one of the most exciting players in Test cricket, with his ability to take on attacking fields setting him apart from several batters around the world.However, while his attacking instincts have won India several matches, they have also come under scrutiny when he has fallen attempting ambitious shots in crucial situations. Questions have therefore persisted over whether Pant can consistently exercise better judgement, particularly when the team finds itself under pressure.India's draw against New Zealand in Wellington once again showcased both sides of the contest. After scoring 128 in the first innings, Pant also made his presence felt behind the stumps as India pushed for a victory on the final day.New Zealand, however, stood firm in their second innings. Starting the fifth day at 119/2, the hosts lost Devon Conway (65) and Rachin Ravindra (37) in the morning session to Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna respectively.India briefly sensed an opportunity, but Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips dug in after lunch. Mitchell remained unbeaten on 24 off 107 balls, while first-innings centurion Phillips made 19 not out off 60 deliveries as the pair added 29 runs in 19 overs.Tom Blundell was the only other wicket to fall in the penultimate session, edging Anshul Kamboj to Pant. New Zealand eventually reached 206/5, with the pitch offering little assistance to the Indian bowlers, as the first Test ended in a draw.Meanwhile, Ashwin also identified Devdutt Padikkal as a major positive for India, praising the left-hander's composure after his 80 off 175 balls in the first innings."For India, the biggest positive from my side in the batting lineup is Devdutt Padikkal," Ashwin said. "I liked his positivity very much. India have been searching for a number three, and they've changed a lot of number threes. He made runs in Sri Lanka, now he's made runs in New Zealand. So I think India have a solid number three in Devdutt."He gives a lot in the field. He's able to move around, shuttle around, rally around with the bowlers. He gives what you expect and he's batting with a lot of composure. I think his competition with Sai Sudarshan is good for Indian cricket."Padikkal's successive contributions in Sri Lanka and New Zealand have strengthened his case for the No. 3 position, according to Ashwin, who believes competition with Sai Sudharsan can only benefit Indian cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England thrash Australia in second T20I as big Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt partnership sparks eight-wicket win
articles.summary: Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt put on a 151-run partnership as England needed just 13.1 overs to beat Australia by eight wickets and level the five-match T20I series; Australia scored 184-8 after winning the toss before England raced to victory
articles.body:
Australia recovered from 84-5 to post 184-8 after winning the toss at Carrara Stadium, with Nikhil Chaudhary (45 from 35) and Joel Davies (39 off 25) offering some late resistance before the hosts added 50 runs from a chaotic final three overs.

Ben Dwarshuis (18 from four) ended the Australian innings by hitting Sam Curran (2-29) for three consecutive sixes, only for Donald and Salt to put England firmly on top with an extraordinary 151-run opening partnership from just 61 deliveries.

Donald threatened the fastest century in England T20 history before being dismissed for 85 from 32 balls, while Salt (58) was removed in the following over by a spectacular caught and bowled from Dwarshuis.

Tom Banton continued the boundary onslaught by finishing 26 not out from eight deliveries, as England raced to their victory target with 41 balls to spare and put the five-match series tied at 1-1 heading into Friday's clash in Brisbane.

England level series with big win in Carrara

Debutant James Coles was handed the new ball after replacing the injured Will Jacks in England's only change, while Mitch Marsh (15) hit Henry Crocombe for successive sixes before chipping straight back to him for the opening Australia wicket.

Jake Fraser-McGurk (27) was free-scoring until he ballooned Curran's first ball to Brook, who took a good catch at long-off, before Coles run out Sam Harper (three) with a diving direct hit from point to leave the host 45-3.

Coles was involved again as he took a routine catch off Craig Overton to remove Tim David (six), while momentum went further England's way when Lachlan Shaw (10) saw his slog sweep off Adil Rashid pick out Salt.

Australia added 49 runs for the sixth wicket until Coles held on to a deep catch off Curran to remove Chaudhary (45), although the hosts looking in danger of an under-par total until they scored 50 runs off a chaotic final three overs.

Jack Edwards made an eight-ball 18 and Davies was run out from the first ball of the final over, while Dwarshuis' remarkable late power-hitting off Curran lifted Australia to 184-8.

Salt was out from the opening ball of the series on Saturday but avoided a repeat in England's chase, where Donald showed an early sign of what was to come by pulling Edwards for successive sixes.

Australia's catching woes that impacted them on Saturday continued when Davies dropped Salt on 11 off Meredith, while Donald smashed Chaudhary for 26 off the next over to race to an 18-ball 50.

Davies' next over went for 31 as Salt crashed in four sixes, bringing up his half-century from 24 deliveries, while Donald looked set to break his partner's record for the fastest T20I ton - standing at 39 balls - until he fell at the start of the 11th over.

Salt's innings ended with a brilliant one-handed catch from Dwarshuis but merely delayed England's victory, as Banton fired two sixes off Adam Zampa before smashing Chaudhary over the leg-side boundary from the opening ball of the next over to complete a one-sided chase.

Brook left 'speechless' by England's batting

England skipper Harry Brook, speaking at the presentation:

"I am speechless. That opening partnership was explosive to say the least.

"The pitch played a bit better than we thought and Salt and Donald put on an absolute clinic. They should be very proud."

Player of the Match, Aneurin Donald, following his 85 off 32 balls:

"It was nice to get going and put on a partnership with a fellow Welshman (Phil Salt) at the top of the order. It was a special day.

"We saw ball and hit ball. Our last partnership was zero so it was nice to get 150 this time. I am new to this level and Salty took the pressure off. His experience was second to none."

England opener Phil Salt, talking to TNT Sports about his opening stand with Donald:

"I felt I hit the ball well but I put on an exhibition of hitting the fielder so as soon as Donald put one away, I fed him the strike. That gave the partnership a chance and, from there, it was good fun - I am over the moon for him.

"I am good now at taking a back seat and choosing my moment to announce myself. It makes it easier when you have someone at the other end hitting it like Donald did. There was not a lot of legwork for me."

Fourth T20I: Sunday November 29 (Sydney)

Fifth T20I: Wednesday December 2 (Canberra)

articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi creates history! Smashes fastest-ever hundred in List A cricket with 28-ball ton
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026,
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, rewriting the List A record books with a sensational century for India A in Doha on Tuesday.The teenage opener smashed a 16-ball half-century before racing to his hundred in just 28 deliveries, registering the fastest century in List A cricket. In the process, Sooryavanshi also became the first batter to score two List A half-centuries in 16 balls or fewer.Sooryavanshi made his intentions clear from the outset, smashing three sixes in the opening over bowled by Zahid Ali. Opening alongside Abhishek Sharma, he helped India A race to 68 runs in just 3.3 overs before Abhishek departed for 12 off five balls.The early dismissal did little to slow Sooryavanshi down, as he continued to attack the UAE bowling attack and brought up his half-century in just 16 deliveries.Fastest List A century (by balls)28 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi India A vs UAE 202629 Jake Fraser-McGurk South Aus vs Tasmania Adelaide 202331 AB de Villiers SA vs WI Joburg 201532 Sakibul Gani Bihar vs Arunachal Ranchi 202533 Ishan Kishan Jharkhand vs Karnataka Ahmedabad 2025The left-hander's assault also helped India A create history as a team. They raced to 100 in just five overs, registering the fastest team century in List A one-day cricket, where ball-by-ball data is available.The previous record belonged to New Zealand, who had reached 100 in 6.3 overs against Sri Lanka in Christchurch in 2015. India A's effort also bettered the 6.3-over mark achieved by India A against Sri Lanka A in Dambulla in 2026 and New Zealand's 6.4-over effort against England in Wellington in 2015.Sooryavanshi's extraordinary knock put him in a league of his own, with his 16-ball fifty adding another milestone to an already remarkable innings.Earlier, UAE had posted 249/8 after being asked to bat first. Former India domestic batter Harpreet Singh Bhatia led their recovery with a career-best 130 off 144 balls, including 12 fours and four sixes.UAE had slipped to 20/2 inside the first six overs after Harshit Rana and Arshad Khan struck early. Harpreet then stitched together important partnerships with Muhammad Shahdad (28) and Ethan D'Souza (25) to rebuild the innings.Arshad finished with four wickets for 43 runs, while Basil Hameed remained unbeaten on 36 off 36 balls to help UAE reach 249/8 in their 50 overs.India A needed 250 runs to win the Group B encounter and secure a place in the semi-finals, but Sooryavanshi's extraordinary start quickly turned the chase into a record-breaking spectacle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia vs England: Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt star as visitors level T20 series
articles.summary: A remarkable opening partnership of 150 in 10 overs between Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt helps England chase 184 against Australia to level the T20 series.
articles.body:
Australia 184-8 (20 overs): Chaudhary 45 (35); Curran 2-29

England 188-2 (13.1 overs): Donald 85 (32); Meredith 1-18

England won by eight wickets; series level 1-1

From Gorseinon to the Gold Coast to global recognition.

Welshman Aneurin Donald's demolition of Australia in the second T20 will make the rest of the world notice his talents and pave the way for numerous franchise deals, according to former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Donald's astonishing opening partnership of 151 in 10 overs with Phil Salt helped England hammer Australia and levelled the T20 series on the Gold Coast, as they chased 184 in just 13.1 overs.

Donald blitzed 85 from 32 balls, including nine sixes, while his compatriot Salt made 58 off 30 as the pair from small Welsh villages in Swansea and Denbighshire took the Australians apart.

Donald's 18-ball fifty was the joint third-fastest for England in the format as the pair raced to 79-0 in the powerplay, flogging Australia's second-string bowling attack to all corners of the ground in a remarkable display of power hitting.

"It was a night where we saw a player really step up to the big stage," Vaughan told BBC Sport.

"I'm sure we're going to see much more over the next few years from Donald, but I think tonight the rest of the world noticed and said 'oh, there's a player there'.

"He's got a few franchise gigs at the moment but to do it on the biggest stage against Australia, with the world watching, he's going to be talked about."

His opening partner Salt, who was dropped by Joel Davies on 10, was mostly able to watch from the non-striker's end before accelerating to a 24-ball half-century of his own, which came during a brutal over from spinner Davies that went for 31.

Donald looked gutted to miss out on a century after he holed out to long-on off Riley Meredith's bowling, before Salt was brilliantly caught and bowled by Ben Dwarshuis an over later.

However, England's phenomenal top order - which still awaits the return of Jos Buttler from injury - finished the job with ease as Tom Banton walked off unbeaten on 26 off eight balls, including a monstrous six for the winning runs.

Australia's 184-8 looked competitive on a surface that had assisted England's spinners and Sam Curran's slower balls - the hosts recovering from a stodgy middle over period after falling to 58-4 in the powerplay.

Davies added a handy cameo of 38 before Dwarshuis whacked Curran's last three balls for six to finish strongly but within just a few overs of the chase, Donald and Salt had silenced a lively Australian crowd in style.

The five-match series continues at the Gabba, Brisbane, on Friday.

England race to emphatic win over Australia inside 14 overs - as it happened

Sooryavanshi, 15, breaks sixes record after scoring 204 off 53 balls

Donald made his T20 international debut as a 29-year-old earlier this summer on the back of consistent county and Hundred performances, but struggled to really cement his place with 56 runs in four innings.

Still, a player known for an incredible strike-rate in particular, he was backed by Harry Brook and Brendon McCullum to play freely and showcased that strength against an Australia attack that had no answers.

"He's the perfect T20 striker," Vaughan added.

"He has got a great base and a good eye and he doesn't over-complicate it. His mindset is to just try and hit everything for six, very much the modern T20 player.

"The game is moving forward and you need players like Donald who can hit the ball like that."

Brook himself said he was "speechless" at the end of the game, high praise from one of the world's best, as Donald and Salt made what could have been a tricky chase look like a stroll in the park.

Only three international T20s had been held at the Gold Coast's Carrara Oval previously so England were in relatively unknown territory.

Not that it mattered to Donald, who swatted Davies for four from his first ball to start the demolition.

His first couple of sixes off Jack Edwards sailed into the crowd despite looking like he had not timed them perfectly, giving Australia captain Mitch Marsh an insight into his new Perth Scorchers team-mate when the Big Bash League starts in December.

Though the pitch had looked difficult to face spin in Australia's innings, Donald and Salt both tucked into it with aplomb - before Salt's takedown of Davies, Donald clubbed Nikhil Chaudhary for 26 to bring up his fifty by the end of the fifth over.

Donald's showcase gives England a nice headache at the top of the order, with Buttler and Jacob Bethell still to come back into the fold - a frightening prospect for opposition bowlers.

Donald aims for England T20 chance in Australia

England's mixed bowling still a cause for concern

Despite the batting brilliance, there were mixed fortunes for England's bowlers with a contrast between their spinners and seamers.

Australia's powerplay was bizarre. Their run-rate was healthy, just shy of 10 runs an over, but they threw away four wickets which meant they had to be more cautious throughout the middle.

Marsh was caught and bowled by Henry Crocombe, Jake Fraser-McGurk was out slogging to Curran before debutant James Coles produced a fine run out to get rid of Sam Harper.

Coles then took the catch in the deep to get rid of Tim David, and that allowed the masterful Adil Rashid and Liam Dawson to get to work, bowling seven overs on the bounce as Australia's middle order came to a standstill.

Rashid tied Lachlan Shaw and Joel Davies in knots early on as they struggled to pick up his variations before he removed the former for a stodgy 10 from 17 balls.

Davies dug in before accelerating at the death, with assistance from the big-hitting Edwards as Jamie Overton's struggles continued.

The 18th over conceded 16 as he only bowled two overs for 28, before Crocombe's penultimate over flew for 16 and Dwarshuis got to work on Curran, who was also taken apart in the final over in Australia's win on Saturday.

Unfortunately for Curran, he had previously been sensational at mixing up his pace deceptively and had figures of 2-9 off his first three, but completely lost control of his yorkers in the final three balls which the powerful Dwarshuis sent flying.

England will be grateful for the return of Jofra Archer to their ranks as their difficulties at closing out an innings are becoming a concern.

articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting, smashing the fastest double century in List A cricket during India A's clash against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Doha on Tuesday.The 15-year-old reached the 200-run mark in just 52 balls, eclipsing the previous record of 103 deliveries held by Chad Bowes, who achieved the feat for Canterbury against Otago in Christchurch in 2024.Sooryavanshi eventually departed for a sensational 204 off just 53 deliveries, having struck seven fours and a staggering 28 sixes. His tally of 28 sixes is the most by any batter in a single List A innings, surpassing D'Arcy Short's previous record of 23 for Western Australia against Queensland in Sydney in 2018. It is also the most sixes hit in a single innings across professional cricket.The teenage sensation rewrote several other records during his extraordinary knock. He brought up his half-century in just 16 balls before reaching his century in a mere 28 deliveries, setting a new record for the fastest List A hundred. The previous record belonged to Jake Fraser-McGurk, who had scored a 29-ball century for South Australia against Tasmania in Adelaide in 2023.Sooryavanshi also reached 150 in just 40 balls, breaking the previous List A record of 64 deliveries held by AB de Villiers, who achieved the feat against the West Indies in Johannesburg in 2015. Mindset was same as every game, wanted to bat long," Sooryavanshi told the host broadcaster.Earlier, UAE had posted 249/8 after being asked to bat first, with former India domestic batter Harpreet Singh Bhatia leading their recovery with an emotional career-best 130 off 144 balls. Having lost two early wickets, Harpreet steadied the innings with crucial partnerships to take UAE to a competitive total.Arshad Khan was the pick of the India A bowlers, claiming four wickets for 43 runs.In reply, India A made light work of the 250-run target, reaching 253/3 in just 14.2 overs to register a seven-wicket victory. Whether facing pace or spin, Sooryavanshi stood his ground and repeatedly sent the ball sailing over the boundary.The emphatic victory was particularly important for India A after their defeat to Pakistan in the previous game. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashes fastest hundred and double century in List A cricket during India A's victory over UAE
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi broke more records on Tuesday as the 15-year-old cricket sensation guided India A to a seven-wicket win vs UAE with an extraordinary knock; the opener made an astounding 204 runs off a mere 53 deliveries, including 28 sixes,
articles.body:
The 15-year-old produced an extraordinary innings, making 204 off a mere 53 deliveries, including 28 sixes, during the Asia Cup Rising Stars group match in Doha.

Sooryavanshi, who became the youngest debutant for India's senior T20 side in July , first raced his way to a 28-ball century, the fastest ton hit in List A cricket, surpassing Jake Fraser-McGurk by one delivery.

The Indian prodigy then went one better, advancing to his second ton off 24 balls to obliterate the record, previously held by Chad Bowes, for the fastest double century struck in List A cricket [103 balls].

His 40-ball 150 was also the fastest in List A cricket too, with the 15-year-old going on to smash four consecutive sixes.

It came after UAE had set India a target of 250 to win and thanks to Sooryavanshi's feats, Tilak Varma's side would go on to seal victory inside 14.2 overs.

Sooryavanshi completed the feat by smashing an incredible 28 sixes and seven fours, with a strike rate of 384.90.

That surpassed Western Australia's D'Arcy Short's record tally of 23 maximums, which he managed during a match against Queensland in 2019.

Known as a ruthless ball striker, Sooryavanshi was named the IPL's MVP for the 2026 season, after leading the league with 776 runs and a strike rate of 237.30.

In February, he set a new record for the highest score made at an Under-19 Cricket World Cup final, making 175 runs from 80 deliveries, as India went on to seal a 100-run win against England.

Sooryavanshi would ultimately be dismissed in the 13th over after he clipped a delivery from Basil Hameed to Aryansh Sharma at long-off.

articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: 15-year-old smashes the record for the fastest List A double century
articles.summary: India's 15-year-old sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blazes 204 from 53 balls for India A, almost halving the record for the fastest double-century in List A cricket.
articles.body:
India's 15-year-old batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit the most sixes ever recorded in a senior men's innings in blazing 204 from 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates.

While almost halving the record for the fastest double-century in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi hit 28 sixes and seven fours in the Asia Cup Rising Stars competition - easily breaking Chad Bowes' previous record of 103 balls from 2024 .

The teenage opener also broke the record for the fastest century and 150, the latter of which he already held, before being caught at long-off with his side five runs from victory.

India A ultimately passed their target of 250, played against a UAE side that featured a number of internationals but was not their current first-choice side, in 14.2 overs in Doha.

Sooryavanshi now holds the following records in List A cricket, the categorisation given to senior one-day matches:

Fastest fifty: 11 balls v Sri Lanka A , 21 June (previously Kaushalya Weeraratne, 12 balls, 1 November 2005)

Fastest hundred: 28 balls, today (previously Jake Fraser-McGurk , 29 balls, 8 October 2023)

Fastest 150: 40 balls, today (previously himself , 59 balls, 24 December 2025)

Fastest 200: 52 balls, today (previously Chad Bowes, 103 balls, 22 October 2024)

The previous record for the most sixes in senior matches was 26, struck by Tanmay Agarwal in an innings of 366 for Hyderabad against Arunachal Pradesh in India's first-class Ranji Trophy competition in January 2024.

The record in List A cricket was 23 sixes, struck by D'Arcy Short for Queensland in his 257 against Tasmania on 28 September 2018.

Sooryavanshi also holds the records of being the youngest century-maker in both List A and T20 cricket and the youngest captain in T20s .

Sooryavanshi, 15, among young stars shaping future

Cartoons & hose hands - what makes Sooryavanshi, 15, special?

The 15-year-old IPL wonderkid ready to play for India

"The first thing that's required in this format is being fearless, he's got plenty of that," former India batter Deep Dasgupta told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"Technically he's quite unique. There is a tendency of being over-coached in this generation, there's so many coaches and when you start playing franchise cricket.

"The best part is he has been fast-tracked so he hasn't had a lot of coaches, he's kind of untouched. What you see of him is predominantly what his natural game is.

"That bat swing, the hand speed, which is very, very natural and one of the quickest you'll come across. Technically he's very gifted, he's very special and he's definitely the real deal."

Sooryavanshi has rapidly become a sensation in T20 cricket since making his debut in the Indian Premier League in 2025 at the age of 14.

He has hit two hundreds and six fifties in his first two seasons in the competition and has earned 10 caps for India in the shortest format since making his debut against England in July.

The left-hander, who was batting in only his 16th List A innings in Doha and made his second century in the format, is yet to play for India in 50-over cricket.

He put on partnerships of 68 with opening partner Abhishek Sharma, who scored 12, 40 with Prabhsimran Singh, who added just three, and 137 with Rinku Singh, who scored an unbeaten 27.

The India A side, which featured a number of internationals, restricted the UAE to 249-8 in 50 overs , external after their opposition had chosen to bat and swiftly reached 254-3 to win by seven wickets and guarantee their place in the semi-finals.

The Rising Stars competition features A sides from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Afghanistan alongside squads from the UAE, Nepal and Hong Kong.

India A, who now top Group B, beat Nepal and lost to Pakistan A in their previous two matches in the competition, with Sooryavanshi making scores of 26 and 11.

Pakistan A will retake the top spot if they beat Nepal on Tuesday, with semi-finals on Thursday and Friday to follow before Sunday's final.

articles.title: Ollie Robinson signs for Nottinghamshire on three-year all-format contract as England bowler ends 11-year spell at Sussex
articles.summary: Former Sussex captain Ollie Robinson has signed a three-year all-format contract with Nottinghamshire; the England seamer has represented Sussex in the County Championship since 2015, taking on the role of red-ball captain in 2026; Robinson had a year left on his Sussex contract
articles.body:
The signing signals the end of an 11-year spell for Robinson at Sussex - whom he captained during the 2026 County Championship Division One season - despite having a year left on his contract.

Robinson joins the 2025 Division One title winners with a stellar first-class record of 520 wickets at an average of 21.09, while boasting 104 wickets at an average of 19.25 for England's Test side.

"I'm absolutely delighted to be joining Nottinghamshire. I've always loved playing at Trent Bridge, and I'm really looking forward to calling it home," Robinson said.

"I have a real desire to win silverware, and with the quality of the squad at Notts, there's no doubt in my mind that we can do that.

"Everyone has told me the environment at Trent Bridge is as close to an international one as you can get, so I'm really excited to see that and make the most of it."

Robinson posted figures of 5-85 in his first and only Test appearance at Trent Bridge, taking 22 first-class wickets in four appearances at the ground, averaging 19.63.

"I'd like to give Sussex a lot of credit throughout this whole process," Nottinghamshire director of cricket Mick Newell added.

"They've been constructive and cordial to deal with, and we're grateful to them for that. We're all thrilled by the statement signing of Ollie, and we know our members and supporters will be too."
