articles.title: Ollie Robinson: England seamer joins Nottinghamshire from Sussex
articles.summary: England seamer Ollie Robinson leaves Sussex after 11 years to join Nottinghamshire for an undisclosed "compensation package" on a three-year deal.
articles.body:
England seamer Ollie Robinson has left Sussex after 11 years to join Nottinghamshire for an undisclosed "compensation package" on a three-year deal.

The 32-year-old had been linked with a move to Trent Bridge for a number of weeks, with confirmation finally coming just three weeks after Robinson was named England's cricketer of the year for 2026 following his remarkable return to the Test team.

After two years in the wilderness, Robinson claimed 28 wickets in four Tests at an average of just 9.30. Before that, he had taken 76 wickets across 20 Test matches between 2021 and 2024.

He captained Sussex in the County Championship last season but because of international commitments he featured in just six red-ball games, taking 18 wickets.

Robinson has said he moves to Notts, a side that took their defence of the County Championship title to the final round of matches last season, with a "real desire to win silverware".

"I have a huge desire to become the very best and hopefully getting some fresh eyes and a new environment, I can maximise my chances of achieving that," he told Nottinghamshire's website. , external

Cricket Media Awards for Robinson, Sharma & Bamber

Farbrace proud as Sussex finish third amid struggles

Sussex, a club that has grappled with financial issues, finished just above Nottinghamshire in the Division One table last season despite having been hit with a 12-point deduction at the start of the campaign because of "sustained operating losses".

The club had a financial framework imposed on them by the English and Wales Cricket Board earlier this year, which came with a spending cap on player salaries. , external

Robinson has taken 520 first-class wickets since he made his County Championship debut for Sussex in 2015.

Before that his professional career comprised of just 10 appearances in limited over matches for Yorkshire, who sacked him , external for a "number of unprofessional actions".

Robinson said it is "incredibly difficult to put into words" what Sussex means to him, having given him a way back into the game and platform to become one of world cricket's most fierce wicket-takers.

"I leave having achieved things I could only have dreamt of when I first walked through the doors, from representing England to having the honour of captaining the club," he added.

"I hope Sussex is proud of everything I have done for them.

"It's not been an easy decision to leave and it's going to feel very strange not walking into the Sussex dressing room next season."

Nottinghamshire head coach Peter Moores says he is "incredibly excited" to have Robinson part of his side at Trent Bridge across all three formats.

"His red-ball record stands up against the very best bowlers in the world," Moores said.

"It feels like he's joining us at a crucial time when we are looking to deepen our red-ball squad to help us be competitive across the whole season."

'Hove will not be the same without him' - analysis

By Adrian Harms, BBC Radio Sussex commentator

Rumours have been circulating for some time on the south coast that Robinson would be joining Notts but, even so, this news will come as yet another hammer blow to beleaguered Sussex supporters.

The four-man seam attack who started the season at Leicester in April has been decimated with only Tom Price remaining, as Robinson, Fynn Hudson-Prentice and Henry Crocombe have all now left the club.

Add to that list the experienced John Simpson and Daniel Hughes, as the guts continues to get ripped out of the Sussex squad, and the full implications of the club's past financial misdemeanours become startling apparent.

But as captain and talisman, the loss of Robinson is the biggest blow, not least as his contract ran for a further year, and raises the question as to whether other players currently under contract, could be heading through the revolving exit door at Hove.

Robinson's record speaks for itself. From scoring a century on his debut against Durham in 2015, to a magnificent haul of 408 first-class wickets at an average of 21.27.

He has bowled the club to victory on numerous occasions but perhaps his performance in taking 9-78 on a flat Cardiff pitch against Glamorgan in 2021will live longest in the memory.

That performance belatedly convinced the England selectors what everyone at Sussex already knew, that Robinson was, and had been for some time, an international class bowler.

His loss cannot be overstated - a student of the game, he showed his leadership qualities in the County Championship last season as Sussex confounded a 12-point deduction by finishing third.

Hove will not be the same without him, bowling down the hill from the Cromwell Road End, beating but more often that not catching the outside edge - this truly is the end of an era.

articles.title: Gloucestershire rebranded as Bristol Lions for T20 Blast
articles.summary: Gloucestershire will rebrand to Bristol Lions for the T20 Blast from the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Gloucestershire will rebrand as Bristol Lions for the T20 Blast from the 2027 season.

The club revealed their intentions earlier this month to change their identity for the format to include Bristol, the city where they play home matches at the Seat Unique Stadium, as part of a strategy to "reach a new audience".

The club, which was founded in 1870, will continue to play County Championship and One-Day Cup matches under the Gloucestershire banner, however, their county crest has also been redesigned as part of the change.

"Gloucestershire County Cricket Club remains unchanged at our core, anchored in over 150 years of heritage," said chief executive officer Neil Priscott.

"Unveiling the Bristol Lions T20 identity is a proactive, strategic step to widen our supporter base across this vibrant city.

"By establishing a modern connection for short-form cricket, we aim to fill stadium seats, engage younger and more diverse audiences, and build financial equity to compete at the highest domestic levels.

"This approach safeguards our history while driving sustainable growth for generations to come."

Gloucestershire to rebrand as Bristol for T20 Blast

Gloucestershire CEO Priscott to step down

Both the men's and women's teams will compete under the Bristol Lions name in the T20 Blast campaigns.

The men have won the title just once in their history - in 2024 when they beat West Country rivals Somerset.

They won seven of their 12 T20 matches in the 2026 season and reached the knockout stage of the tournament, while the women's team have competed in Tier 2 of the competition since it was restructured two years ago.

Since being relegated to Division Two of the County Championship in 2022, Gloucestershire have finished bottom in two of the past four seasons, including this summer when they won three of 14 matches.

"We want to consistently compete as a top eight county across all formats," said director of cricket Jon Lewis.

"The T20 format demands intensity, energy, modern presentation and a powerful connection with the crowd.

"Establishing the Bristol Lions identity gives our players a powerful platform to build on, exciting current fans while inspiring a new generation of players and supporters across the region."

A club statement said that the rebrand to Bristol Lions would help "accelerate commercial revenues" and "secure long-term financial sustainability, to directly reinvest back into cricket across all formats".

Warwickshire previously rebranded to Birmingham Bears for the Blast in 2014, also targeting a new audience.

While they said they saw attendances grow during that time, the decision was taken before the start of the 2026 season to reverse the change and return to Warwickshire.

"With our long-term future in mind, and following feedback from members through the members' committee, now is the right time for change," said chief executive Stuart Cain.

"We represent the county, and that's what returning to Warwickshire Bears is about."

Gloucestershire have played at the historic Bristol County Ground in Ashley Down, Bristol, for more than a century, with the first match held on Nevil Road in 1889.

In December 2023 it was confirmed the club were exploring options to relocate to a new site on the edge of the city.

And in April last year they signed a non-binding head of terms agreement to explore a new site in Swanmoor Stoke , situated in the north west outskirts of Bristol near the M5 and M49 motorways.

articles.title: How all-Welsh pairing of Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt delivered 'unbelievable' T20 win as England thrash Australia
articles.summary: England's all-Welsh opening partnership of Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt delivered a 151-run opening partnership as Harry Brook's side raced to an eight-wicket victory; Donald fired 85 from just 32 deliveries to help England race to their target
articles.body:
Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt combined for a 151-run opening stand in just 61 deliveries, firing 13 sixes along the way, as England raced to their victory target of 185 inside just 13.1 overs.

Donald declared himself "quite good at slogging" after smashing 85 in just 32 balls, where he threatened to break Salt's record as England's fastest T20 centurion before hitting Riley Meredith to long-on.

Salt scored four sixes in one 31-run Joel Davies over and was on 58 when he was out caught-and-bowled to Ben Dwarshuis, with the Welsh duo laying the firm foundations to close out an eight-wicket win.

"Speechless, just unbelievable," Brook said of his power-hitting opening pair. "That opening partnership was explosive to say the least.

"The pitch played a bit better than we thought and Salt and Donald put on an absolute clinic. They should be very proud."

Donald only scored 56 runs from his first four England outings but ended that disappointing run in spectacular fashion in Carrara, with his strike-rate of 216.37 making him the fastest run-scorer in all T20 cricket since the start of 2024.

"It was pretty special doing that with Salty, two proud Welshmen ticking the box for the England and Wales Cricket Board. We'll mention it a lot more now," Donald admitted, having been named player of the match.

"There's not many sports where you play as two nations together. Wales probably hasn't produced the guys they'd have liked to after having some good youngsters over the years. It's special and it's testament to the system back home.

"Welsh cricket and the support I've had in my career has been incredible and it feels like this is a night where I can give back a little bit."

'I'm quite good at slogging' - Donald savours special innings

Donald's free-flowing innings was further proof that he could deliver on the big stage, with Australian captain Mitch Marsh looking forward to playing with the Welshman when he features for Perth Scorchers in the Big Bash after this series.

"Donald is my opening partner at the Perth Scorchers this season so I am looking forward to watching that from the other end!" Marsh admitted.

"I thought we were well in the game posting 184 but hats off to England - we tried everything and some of our good balls were going 40 rows back. We were under extreme pressure."

Donald's 18-ball fifty was the joint third-fastest for England in the format, with his latest knock likely to attract further interest from Indian Premier League franchises ahead of the auction next month for the 2027 season.

"In the last few years I've realised I'm not great at batting but I'm quite good at slogging," Donald added. "In modern cricket I'm not sure there's too much (of a difference), especially in T20, but there might be a career in it now.

"It's just about staying true to myself and trusting that bat swing. I'm sure I'm going to make myself look like an idiot over the next few years batting the way I do, but hopefully it's going to come off more often than not.

"I'm not the most skilful, I'm not the most powerful but my intent and the way I play has probably separated me out in the last few months. There's going to be periods where it's not quite firing but it's about staying as true as I can."
